chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Aḥmad ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:
Indeed, Allah, when He loves a servant, immerses him in affliction thoroughly; and indeed we and you, O Sudayr, enter the morning with it and enter the evening with it.

key_terms.أَحَبَّ: loved; indicates Allah’s special care and favor toward a servant
key_terms.بِالْبَلَاءِ: with affliction; trials and hardships sent upon a person
key_terms.عَبْدًا: a servant; the human being in relation to Allah as His servant
key_terms.غَتًّا: thoroughly immersing; an intense engulfing in trial
key_terms.لَنُصْبِحُ: we enter the morning; points to continual experience of affliction
key_terms.وَنُمْسِي: we enter the evening; indicates persistence of trials throughout one’s state

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah afflict those whom He loves?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that affliction can be a sign of Allah’s love for His servant, not a sign of abandonment. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام also states that he and the believers, such as Sudayr, continually experience such trials, indicating the ongoing spiritual reality of testing.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ahmad Bin Ubeyd, from Al Husayn  Bin Alwan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said, and in his<sup>asws</sup> presence was Sadeyr:
Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, when He<sup>azwj</sup> Loves a servant Immerses him in the afflictions with an immersion, and I<sup>asws</sup> and you all, O Sadeyr, are with it, in the morning and evening’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ahmad ibn ‘Ubayd from al-Husayn ibn ‘Ulwan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
when the Imam said, ‘When Allah loves a servant He deeply immerses him in misfortunes. You and we, O Sadir, live in it mornings and evenings.’”
